name: upgauge-api-rate-limit
description: THE THRESHOLD (issue #19's third acceptance criterion, #52's second option, widened off /api/ by #83, onto three entity prefixes by #113 and onto /route/ by #117): block a source IP once it exceeds 1 request/second on any path that reaches the origin uncached, blocking for 10 seconds. /api/pivot and /explore share the residual `f` axis that lib/canonicalQuery.ts and lib/pivot/bounds.ts deliberately leave open BECAUSE this rule was said to cover it -- it did not cover /explore until #83, so that reasoning was load-bearing on a rule that was not there. The four */opengraph-image paths are the most expensive request on the site: a DuckDB query plus a rasterize, with no warm path at the origin. /airport/, /carrier/ and /aircraft/ each carry a query key -- ?y=, ?type=, ?carrier= -- whose REFUSED value is no-store and renders in full at the origin, measured at 82-104 ms against 0.9-1.6 ms for the 307 strip, over an unbounded value space. /route/ is in for a DIFFERENT reason (#117): it carries no query key at all (keys: NO_KEYS), so it has no refused-value family -- its residual is a 404 space, where an unknown pair is a no-store 404 that runs the site's largest query TWICE (proxy, then not-found.tsx's reason) with no CDN absorption, over an unbounded URL space. That is a worse per-request shape than the family #113 closed, not a smaller one. http.request.uri.path carries no query string, so matching that family matches those prefixes' cached 200s with it: an entity page view draws on this bucket too, which is affordable only because DataTable emits a plain anchor and TopBar pins prefetch=false, making a page view ONE request here with every asset it pulls under /_next/. MEASURED 2026-08-27 on the served /route/JFK-LAX: 5 serialized Link refs against 5 prefetch=false props (1:1, so none takes the prefetching default), 10 /_next/ assets and one /favicon.ico -- one slot per view, the same arithmetic #113 rested on. The threshold stays 10-per-10s because that measurement holds for /route/ too; the accepted consequence is that a visitor middle-clicking ten route links into background tabs inside ten seconds trips the rule and is blocked for ten. /_next/ is out and stays out: assets are immutable and a single real page load asks for more static chunks than 1/s allows, so widening this to a bare / prefix would throttle every genuine visitor. /search reaches the origin uncached and is NOT matched; it is named as uncovered in docs/architecture/hosting.md rather than implied. The trailing ends_with clause is now a BACKSTOP rather than load-bearing: all four opengraph-image routes sit under the four entity prefixes, so it matches nothing they do not, and it is kept because that redundancy lasts only while all four stay covered -- test_cloudflare_desired_state.py strikes the prefixes out and re-asks, which is the only thing that would notice its deletion. robots.txt already disallows /api/ to well-behaved crawlers; this is the backstop for ones that ignore it. The window is 10s because this zone's plan permits no other: the API rejects anything else with 'not entitled to use the period 60, can only use a period among [10]'. The design asked for 60-per-60s; that is the same sustained rate, but 10-in-10s trips on a burst 60-in-60s would have absorbed. The mitigation timeout is 10s for the same reason as the window: 'not entitled to use a mitigation timeout different from 10'. The design asked to block for 60s, so a throttled client resumes six times sooner than intended -- this caps sustained throughput, it is not a wall.

rules.description: Rate limit the uncached origin paths -- /api/, /explore, the four entity prefixes, and the OG cards -- to 1 request/second per source IP so a scraper cannot keep the origin busy
rules.expression: (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/api/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/explore") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/route/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/airport/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/carrier/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/aircraft/") or ends_with(http.request.uri.path, "/opengraph-image"))
